newsitem.title: KENYA: Overall inflation seen marginally down in Kenya.
newsitem.headline: Overall inflation seen marginally down in Kenya.

text.p: Kenya's annualised inflation based on a three-month average declined to 32.5 percent in April compared to 35.6 percent in March, the Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) said on Wednesday.
Month-on-month inflation rose to 16.1 percent in April from 15.6 percent in March while average annual inflation rose to 11.5 percent, CBK Chief Economist Maurice Kanga said in a statement.
Monthly inflation was 7.3 percent in April 1996.
"The overall month-on-month and annual average inflation continued to rise, again due to the drought effects, but at a much subdued pace," Kanga said.
Last year, short rains (in October to December) failed in most parts of Kenya. Drought persisted in key crop growing areas until late March when seasonal long rains arrived.
The shortage of rains has meant a sharp rise in prices of staple foods, such as maize flour, kale and beans.
"The upward trend in overall inflation is beginning to ease as the supply of food items begins to return to normal following the long rains," Kanga said.
"We forecast overall inflation to continue declining as the food supply situation improves. We forecast underlying inflation to remain at single digits throughout 1997," Kanga added.
Underlying inflation ignores fluctuations caused by temporary setbacks such as drought.

Underlying three-months annualised inflation fell to 2.8 percent in April from 4.0 percent while underlying month-on-month inflation declined to 7.1 percent from 7.3 percent in that period, according to figures issued by Kanga.
